sections.h2: Does Idaho have an estate tax or an inheritance tax?
sections.html:
No. The Idaho State Tax Commission states that Idaho has no gift tax or inheritance tax, and that its estate tax expired in 2004. The estate tax rules it still describes apply only to deaths before January 1, 2005.

For an heir selling a house in Idaho, that means no state death tax is due on the transfer itself. The Commission's estates and taxes page gives a Boise-area number, (208) 334-7660, and a toll-free number, (800) 972-7660, for questions about deaths before 2005.

Other taxes can still touch an inherited house: federal estate tax for very large estates, income tax on a gain after the sale, and the property tax bill that continues to arrive while the estate is open.

sections.h2: When does the federal estate tax apply?
sections.html:
Federal estate tax is a concern only for estates above the basic exclusion amount, which the IRS lists as $15,000,000 for people who die in 2026. The same figure is the filing threshold for the year of death.

ItemAmount (2026)Source
Basic exclusion amount$15,000,000IRS, What's new, estate and gift tax
Estate tax filing threshold$15,000,000IRS, estate tax
Annual gift exclusion per donee$19,000IRS, What's new, estate and gift tax

Source: IRS, What's new, estate and gift tax. The IRS attributes the 2026 figure to the Working Families Tax Cuts law, so confirm the amount for the year of death.

The threshold applies to the whole estate, not the house alone. Executors add up real estate, accounts, business interests and other assets to see whether a federal return is needed.

sections.h2: How does an heir's basis work when an Idaho house is sold?
sections.html:
An heir generally takes a basis equal to the property's fair market value on the date of the owner's death, according to IRS Publication 551. Gain is measured from that value, not from what the original owner paid decades earlier.

  • If the house sells soon after death at about the date-of-death value, the gain is small.
  • If it is held and the market rises, the gain above the date-of-death value is taxable.
  • If the decedent received the property as a gift within a year before death, a different rule can apply.
  • A written appraisal as of the date of death is useful support for the figure.

If you then sell in Idaho, our Idaho capital gains guide explains the state's 60% deduction for qualifying real property held 12 months. Ask a tax professional how the 12-month holding period is counted for inherited property.

sections.h2: Who can sell an inherited house in Idaho?
sections.html:
The personal representative appointed by the court can sell it. Idaho Code 15-3-711 gives a personal representative the same power over title to estate property that an absolute owner would have, held in trust for the people entitled to it, and the section 15-3-715 list of authorized transactions includes selling, mortgaging or leasing real or personal property of the estate.

The same section allows a personal representative to:

  • dispose of land, in Idaho or another state, for cash or on credit, at public or private sale;
  • make ordinary or extraordinary repairs to buildings;
  • pay taxes, assessments and the costs of administration;
  • hire attorneys, auditors or agents to help.

These powers are subject to limits in the will or in a court order, so a will that restricts sale changes the answer. Idaho Code 15-3-714 also protects a person who deals with a personal representative, since a limiting provision is effective only against those with actual knowledge of it.

sections.h2: What about the small estate affidavit?
sections.html:
Idaho Code 15-3-1201 lets a successor collect certain assets by affidavit when the probate estate is worth $100,000 or less, but its text does not mention real estate. It applies after 30 days have passed since death, and only if no petition for a personal representative is pending or granted anywhere.

The statute names payment of debts, tangible personal property, instruments of debt and securities. A house is therefore not clearly within this shortcut. Ask the title company which documents it needs to close, and speak to a probate attorney if the estate is under the threshold but holds real property.

The affidavit must state that the fair market value of the entire estate subject to probate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000. The Department of Health and Welfare is treated as a successor for medical assistance recovery in some cases, under subsection (c). Our Idaho probate guide explains the court route in full.

sections.h2: Which Idaho statutes govern an estate sale?
sections.html:
Estate administration is in Title 15 of the Idaho Code, the Uniform Probate Code, Chapter 3, which covers probate of wills and administration. The chapter is organized in parts that matter to a house sale.

PartSubject
Part 7Duties and powers of personal representatives
Part 10Closing estates
Part 11Compromise of controversies
Part 12Collection of personal property by affidavit and summary procedure for small estates
Part 13Uniform estate tax apportionment

Source: Idaho Legislature, Title 15, Chapter 3. Part 13 exists to apportion estate tax among recipients, which does not create a state tax.

A lifetime transfer is a different question. Idaho has no gift tax, and the federal annual exclusion is $19,000 per recipient for 2026. A gift of real estate worth more than that amount is a federal question to raise with a tax professional. Our Idaho quitclaim deed guide covers the deed itself.

sections.h2: What costs should an Idaho heir expect while the house is unsold?
sections.html:
The estate remains responsible for property tax, insurance and upkeep from the date of death until closing. County rules are the same as for any owner. In Ada County, for example, the first half is due December 20 and the second half June 20, with a 2% late charge and monthly interest on a late payment.

Section 15-3-715 lets the personal representative pay taxes and administration expenses from estate funds. The homeowner's exemption lasts until ownership changes or the home stops being a primary residence, according to the state, so ask the county Assessor whether it continues after a death.

Our Idaho property tax guide and the county guides for Ada and Canyon list the assessor and treasurer offices.

sections.h2: What do heirs in Idaho commonly face?
sections.html:
An inherited house that sits vacant still generates property tax, utilities and insurance costs, and any will restriction or court order has to be sorted out before a sale.

We buy houses as is in Idaho, including inherited ones, so cleanout and repairs do not need to come first. Call or text for a written cash offer. If you decline it, you owe us nothing. Before accepting any offer, make sure the personal representative has the authority described above and a licensed attorney has reviewed the estate documents.

faqs.q: Does Idaho have an inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. The Idaho State Tax Commission says Idaho has no gift tax or inheritance tax, and its estate tax expired in 2004.

faqs.q: Do I owe tax when I inherit a house in Idaho?
faqs.a: Idaho does not tax the inheritance itself. You may owe income tax on a gain if you later sell for more than the date-of-death value.

faqs.q: What is the federal estate tax exemption for 2026?
faqs.a: The IRS lists a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000 for people who die in 2026, and the filing threshold is the same.

faqs.q: Can a personal representative sell real estate without court approval?
faqs.a: Idaho Code 15-3-715 lets a personal representative sell estate real property unless the will or a court order restricts it, so check both.

faqs.q: Is a small estate affidavit enough to sell a house?
faqs.a: Probably not. Idaho Code 15-3-1201 covers payment of debts, tangible personal property, instruments and securities for estates of $100,000 or less, and it does not name real estate.
